title: Logistics Data Bank Tracks 10 Crore EXIM Containers, Provides Visibility across Logistics Chain
subtitle: Efficient Logistics Central to Strengthening Manufacturing and Expanding Global Markets: Union Minister of Commerce & Industry Shri Piyush Goyal
body_text:
The Logistics Data Bank (LDB) has tracked 10 crore EXIM containers since its launch in 2016. The platform provides visibility of EXIM container movement across the country through technology-based tracking systems. LDB supports visibility across the logistics chain and provides information to stakeholders to facilitate monitoring of container movement.
Speaking on the occasion, Union Minister of Commerce & Industry, Shri Piyush Goyal said: “The tracking of 10 crore containers through the Logistics Data Bank is an important milestone in India’s logistics journey. Technology is helping us make logistics simpler, faster and more efficient, while improving the competitiveness of Indian industry. Efficient logistics will be central to strengthening manufacturing, expanding our presence in global markets and realizing the Hon’ble Prime Minister’s vision of a Viksit Bharat.”
LDB provides visibility of 100 per cent of India’s EXIM container movement through RFID-based technology, covering 19 ports and 32 container terminals. Its network also extends to 103 Inland Container Depots, 439 Container Freight Stations, Empty Yards, Parking Plazas and Industrial Zones, 89 Manufacturing Special Economic Zones, 5,569 railway stations, 269 toll plazas and three Integrated Check Posts.
The platform provides analytics on dwell time, transit time, and port and terminal performance, enabling stakeholders to monitor logistics operations and identify bottlenecks.
LDB 2.0, launched by Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal in September 2025, expanded the platform’s capabilities by enabling high-seas tracking of India’s export containers and providing multimodal shipment visibility.
LDB uses Radio Frequency Identification (RFID), Internet of Things (IoT), Big Data and Cloud technologies to track containers across ports, rail networks, industrial zones, borders and highways, providing near real-time visibility of container movement across the logistics chain. The World Bank’s Logistics Performance Index (LPI) has also recognised the role of LDB in India’s logistics performance.
Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director, National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation (NICDC), and Chairman, NICDC Logistics Data Services Limited (NLDSL), Shri Rajat Kumar Saini, IAS, said, “Reaching 10 crore containers is a proud moment in the journey of LDB. What began with the objective of bringing visibility to EXIM container movement has today become an important digital platform for India’s logistics sector. This achievement has been possible through the continued cooperation of the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, ports, terminals, CFSs, ICDs and our other stakeholders. As we look ahead, our endeavour will be to further strengthen LDB through analytics and new technologies to meet the evolving needs of India’s logistics sector.”
LDB has an average of over 1.5 crore container searches every month. Its container tracking services are available through a single-window platform at www.ldb.co.in, enabling stakeholders to track containers.
NICDC Logistics Data Services Limited (NLDSL) works on logistics technology solutions including the Logistics Data Bank and Unified Logistics Interface Platform (ULIP). These platforms use digital technologies to support efficiency, transparency and digitisation in the logistics sector.
NLDSL was established on 30 December 2015 with the objective of harnessing Information and Communication Technology (ICT) to enhance efficiency in the Indian logistics sector. It is a joint venture between the Government of India, represented by the National Industrial Corridor Development and Implementation Trust (NICDIT), and Japanese IT major NEC Corporation.

Abhishek Dayal/Anushka Pandey

enrichment.summary: The Logistics Data Bank (LDB), a digital tracking platform launched in 2016, has tracked 10 crore EXIM containers using RFID-based technology across 19 ports, 32 container terminals and other logistics nodes nationwide. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal called this a milestone in India's logistics journey, emphasising technology's role in improving efficiency and industrial competitiveness. The platform, operated by NICDC Logistics Data Services Limited (NLDSL), was upgraded to LDB 2.0 in September 2025 to include high-seas tracking and multimodal shipment visibility.
enrichment.context:
The Logistics Data Bank is part of India's broader push to digitise and streamline its logistics ecosystem, complementing the National Logistics Policy (2022) and the Unified Logistics Interface Platform (ULIP), both aimed at reducing logistics costs (historically estimated at 13-14% of GDP, among the highest globally) and improving India's ranking on the World Bank's Logistics Performance Index. LDB, run by NLDSL—a joint venture between the Government of India (via NICDIT) and Japan's NEC Corporation—uses RFID, IoT, Big Data and Cloud technologies to provide real-time visibility of container movement, addressing long-standing inefficiencies caused by fragmented tracking across ports, railways, and road networks.

This announcement is essentially a progress milestone (10 crore containers tracked) rather than a new policy or scheme, but it underscores the government's continuing emphasis on logistics efficiency as a lever for manufacturing competitiveness and export growth, tying into the 'Viksit Bharat' vision and initiatives like PM Gati Shakti, which similarly seeks integrated infrastructure planning through digital data platforms.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Logistics Data Bank' (LDB), recently in the news, is associated with which of the following?
options: Tracking of EXIM container movement using RFID-based technology
A digital ledger for GST refunds on exports
A financial inclusion database for MSMEs
prelims_questions.explanation: The Logistics Data Bank tracks EXIM (export-import) container movement across India's ports, terminals, ICDs, and other logistics nodes using RFID-based technology, providing near real-time visibility of the logistics chain.

prelims_questions.question: NICDC Logistics Data Services Limited (NLDSL), which operates the Logistics Data Bank, is a joint venture between the Government of India and which foreign entity?
prelims_questions.explanation: NLDSL was established in 2015 as a joint venture between the Government of India (through NICDIT) and Japan's NEC Corporation to enhance ICT-driven efficiency in India's logistics sector.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the role of digital technologies such as RFID, IoT, and Big Data in improving logistics efficiency in India. How do platforms like the Logistics Data Bank and Unified Logistics Interface Platform (ULIP) support the objectives of the National Logistics Policy?
mains_questions.gs_paper: GS Paper 3 - Economy: Infrastructure and Logistics

mains_questions.question: High logistics costs have historically been a drag on India's export competitiveness. Evaluate the steps taken by the government to reduce logistics costs and improve supply chain visibility, and suggest further measures needed.
mains_questions.gs_paper: GS Paper 3 - Economy: Growth and Development

study_notes.reason: The release is essentially a factual progress milestone naming a specific institution (LDB/NLDSL), its ownership structure, technology stack and its parent platform (ULIP) and metric (LPI) - all of which are clean objective-question material - while the analytical content (logistics cost reduction, competitiveness) is generic framing rather than substantive new argument.

prelims.point: Logistics Data Bank (LDB) is operated by NICDC Logistics Data Services Limited (NLDSL), a joint venture between the Government of India (via NICDIT) and Japan's NEC Corporation, established December 2015; LDB launched 2016.
prelims.why_important: Institutional ownership structure of a GoI digital logistics platform, including the specific foreign JV partner, is a classic prelims distractor point.

prelims.point: Unified Logistics Interface Platform (ULIP) is another digital platform run by NLDSL, distinct from but complementary to LDB.
prelims.why_important: UPSC often tests distinctions between similarly-named logistics digitisation initiatives under the National Logistics Policy framework.

prelims.point: LDB uses RFID, IoT, Big Data and Cloud technologies for near real-time tracking of EXIM containers across ports, rail, road and industrial zones.
prelims.why_important: Tests knowledge of which specific technologies underpin India's flagship logistics tracking system.

prelims.point: World Bank's Logistics Performance Index (LPI) has recognised LDB's role in India's logistics performance.
prelims.why_important: Links a domestic platform to an internationally published index, a common prelims connection UPSC likes to test.

prelims.point: LDB 2.0, launched September 2025, added high-seas tracking of export containers and multimodal shipment visibility.
prelims.why_important: Recent upgrades to existing schemes are frequently tested to check currency of preparation.

mains.point: Digital tracking platforms like LDB address fragmented, opaque logistics chains and aim to reduce India's high logistics cost (historically ~13-14% of GDP), directly supporting manufacturing competitiveness and export growth.
mains.analytical_use: Useful for answers on measures to improve India's logistics performance or reduce logistics costs as a share of GDP.

mains.point: Multi-agency coordination (Ports, Shipping and Waterways; Road Transport and Highways; ports; terminals; ICDs) needed to sustain a nationwide tracking platform highlights governance and interoperability challenges in infrastructure digitisation.
mains.analytical_use: Can be deployed in questions on challenges of inter-ministerial coordination in implementing pan-India digital infrastructure projects.

low_priority.point: Minister's and NICDC Chairman's laudatory quotes on the milestone
low_priority.reason: Political rhetoric without new policy substance or analytical content.

low_priority.point: Granular node counts (19 ports, 32 terminals, 103 ICDs, 439 CFSs, 5,569 railway stations, 269 toll plazas, 3 ICPs)
low_priority.reason: Excessive operational detail with no standalone significance beyond illustrating scale; unlikely to be tested precisely.

low_priority.point: Average of 1.5 crore container searches per month on the LDB portal
low_priority.reason: A usage statistic without independent analytical or testable significance.
